title: R11: lore check enforces lore validate's required sections and required fields for every type (lore minor release, behaviour change)
description: Binding record: opum-doc main 7818aca8b, docs/adr/add-constitution-and-constants-document-types-to-lore.md, Amendment 1, R11 and its Rollout order (ODOC-288, commit 501ece4ed, opum-ai/opum-doc#460; opum-agent OPAG-425). Read it there before implementing. The rule: lore check enforces the required sections and required fields that lore validate enforces, for EVERY type, not only Constitution and Constants. Reason: lore check exit 0 is the fleet's definition of done, and a rule only validate runs is one no gate runs. Measured cost (LCLI-598, lore c956cca6): 1 of 384 fleet documents, opum-doc's chart-a-graph-primitives-roadmap Story. ROLLOUT ORDER: (1) opum-doc fixes that Story first. DONE: verified on opum-doc main 7818aca8b, where the Story now has '## Acceptance criteria'. (2) lore-cli ships enforcement in a lore MINOR release, with a CHANGELOG entry marking it a behaviour change for external users and naming lore validate as the way to preview the findings before upgrading. No evidence of external breakage exists (external npm users cannot be measured), so the amendment rules hard enforcement, not a warning. Design facts from LCLI-598: check enforces no required sections today, even for fully parsed files, since the tasks: carve-out only governs fields; and check fully parses only files carrying tasks:. Build on LCLI-595's check-side call site (src/commands/check.ts beside the per-file type peek; opum-ai/lore-cli#296) rather than a second mechanism, and keep original rule names (required-section, frontmatter) in check's findings. Re-measure fleet impact by ref just before merging, using LCLI-598's recorded method; the count may have moved.

acceptanceCriteria.text: lore check fails a document of ANY type missing a required section or a required field that lore validate reports, with validate's rule names, proven by tests over existing types (ADR, Story, and a profile-required field on a document without tasks:)
A fleet re-measurement by ref just before merge, using LCLI-598's method, is recorded here, and any newly failing fleet document is routed to its owner before release
The CHANGELOG entry for the lore minor release that ships it marks it a behaviour change and names lore validate as the preview; bun test and bun run lore check exit 0

implementationNotes: IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-26 on branch feat/LCLI-606-check-enforces-required (from origin/dev 3b268813), lore from source, quest 0.10.0, bun 1.3.14. DESIGN: no second mechanism. LCLI-595's check-side call site in tryConceptsForBundle (src/commands/check.ts), beside the per-file type peek, now runs for EVERY file with frontmatter instead of registered types only (renamed typeShapeCheckFindings -> validateRuleCheckFindings). It reuses validateConceptText and keeps, under validate's own rule names, error-tier 'frontmatter' (missing type, missing/mistyped required field, stray second fence), 'required-section', and registered types' 'type-shape'. Files validate skips (no frontmatter) yield nothing. TASKS: DEDUPE: parseConcept on a tasks: file is now wrapped; when it throws a LoreError whose message equals a 'frontmatter' finding already emitted for that file (reportsSameDefect, exact-message match), the file is left out of reconciliation and the throw is NOT raised. Any other throw is carried as before. BEHAVIOUR CHANGE for tasks: files with invalid frontmatter: before = no finding, runCheck rejected with the first such error only (stderr error envelope, complete:false), exit 6; after = one ordinary 'frontmatter' finding per defective file, complete:true, exit 6, no thrown error, run may stay synchronous. Exit code unchanged; --json shape unchanged (new values of the existing rule field). Unparseable YAML is unchanged: it still throws earlier, in the link pass. A tasks: Story missing only a section is still reconciled (drift still reported) and draws required-section. Cosmetic divergence kept: check's frontmatter message embeds the bundle-relative path (check's file convention), validate's the repo-relative one; the LCLI-595 site already behaved so.

TESTS: new test/check-required-rules.test.ts (7): [section] ADR missing ## Consequences; [section] Story missing ## Acceptance criteria; [field] profile-required 'owner' missing on a Reference with no tasks: (.lore/profile.toml in the bundle); [field] frontmatter with no type; each asserts exit 6 AND check's findings for the file == lore validate's error findings under that rule (real runValidate over the same bundle, path prefix normalised). Controls: fixed ADR+Story+typed file exit 0 no findings; Reference with owner exit 0; no-frontmatter file skipped by validate and not flagged by check. check.test.ts: +1 [section] tasks:-linked Story missing its section -> required-section AND status-drift, complete:true. Rewritten to the new mechanism, same invariants: 7 LORE-27/LORE-50/LORE-89 tests that pinned the malformed-tasks: rejection. Fixtures given ## Acceptance criteria: storyDoc helper (test/helpers.ts) + 2 inline Stories. schema-drift.test.ts's async-escalation test re-triggered by a missing managed task region (a 6-class async rejection with no Backlog IO) instead of a malformed linked concept. MUTATION (predicted in writing before each run, full suite): S = drop required-section from the filter -> predicted 6 red, observed exactly those 6 (2 [section] new, 1 [section] tasks: Story, 3 Constitution missing-section); every [field] test green. F = drop frontmatter -> predicted 16 red, observed 17: all 16 predicted + LCLI-595's 'control: the BUILT-IN Constitution still gets every rule' (asserts check draws frontmatter; a field-side test my prediction missed because I read only helper-based describes). No [section] test went red. F also produced 3 unhandled rejections: the old parseConcept throw returning under the mutant, expected. TIMING bun run lore check on this repo: sequential baseline median 11.785s (7 runs); interleaved A/B swapping origin/dev check.ts vs this one, 8 rounds each: before median 11.277s / mean 11.543s, after median 11.391s / mean 11.506s -> within noise. Marginal cost in-process: validateConceptText over all 82 docs files 58.2 ms per pass (0.71 ms/file). GATES: bun test 3740 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail; bun run lore check exit 0 (82 files, 0 errors) with a positive control on this repo (ADR-0007's Consequences heading renamed -> exit 6, exactly one required-section finding; restored byte-identical); typecheck exit 0; biome check on the 5 changed code files exit 0. No lore-cli doc needed fixing: lore validate on this repo was already 0 errors / 82 files. AC2 (fleet re-measurement) left to the parent session.

AC1 checked on: test/check-required-rules.test.ts [section] ADR/Story and [field] profile-field-without-tasks/no-type tests, each run through the real lore check AND lore validate with exit 6 and identical rule+message, plus controls; and a positive control on this repo's own bundle (renamed ADR-0007 Consequences -> exit 6, one required-section finding). AC3 checked on: CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] > Changed entry marked BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, naming lore validate as the preview and stating it ships in a minor release; bun test exit 0 (3740 pass, 0 fail) and bun run lore check exit 0. RESIDUAL for release time, not yet satisfiable: the version that ships this entry must be a MINOR bump (0.9.3 -> 0.10.0); confirm at tag cut.

REVIEW FOLLOW-UP (second commit, after merging origin/dev 53d8912d; review of fcbf5d95). S1: docs (CHANGELOG, cli-surface, cli-contract, okf-conformance, ADR-0007 amendment) now name exactly what check enforces: every error-tier 'frontmatter' and 'required-section' finding validate reports (missing sections, missing type, missing or mistyped fields, invalid enum values e.g. OKF 0.2 lifecycle status), 'lore validate' as the preview. Deliberately NOT 'validate's whole error tier': validate's error-severity 'quote-safety' findings are not enforced by check, so that wording would be false; widening to them needs the scope ruling. S2: check's per-file rules now take validate's exact inputs: the REPO-relative path (toRepoRelative(root, root/label/file)) and a ValidateJudge resolved once per run = loadBundleState(docs/) + profileForBundle(configured profile, that state). This covers (a) a scoped check in an OKF 0.2 bundle, (b) a scoped root's index.md mistaken for the bundle-root index, and (c) docs/docs/index.md compared bundle-relative against ROOT_INDEX_PATH. If docs/index.md yields no usable state (validate refuses to judge), each root falls back to its own state as before. Messages are now byte-identical to validate's. The tasks: dedupe re-spells the throw's ' in <bundle-path>' as ' in <repo-path>' before the exact-message compare. Tests [agree a/b/c] in check-required-rules.test.ts assert both gates exit 6 with identical findings; against fcbf5d95's check.ts all three went red with check exit 0 vs 6. S4: the stray second fence was reported twice; double-frontmatter is a released contract name (CHANGELOG 0.4.0, LCLI-372), so check keeps it and drops validate's frontmatter copy (exact match on a new shared strayFenceMessage builder in core/validate, which core/check now uses too; bytes unchanged). Tested: one finding, rule double-frontmatter. S3: scan-error fixture = bundle-root docs/index.md carrying tasks: [] under a profile requiring owner on Reference (validate judges the root index by the built-in profile: clean; check's reconciliation parse uses the bundle profile: throws; no finding names it, so it is carried). 7 [scan-error] tests in check.test.ts (carried as the run's error with complete:false; report before rejection; advisories before report; same-root isolation; per-root isolation; LORE-50 first-scan-error-wins over a later root's config failure; NOT suppressed when the file's finding names a different defect) + 1 exit-7 escalation test in schema-drift.test.ts.

MUTATIONS round 2 (predicted in writing before each run, full suite, check.ts restored byte-identical after each): M1 carry->throw: predicted 8, got exactly those 8 (7 [scan-error] + the schema-drift escalation). M2 reportsSameDefect always true: predicted the same 8, got the same 8. M2' ignore the message (suppress on any frontmatter finding): predicted 1, got 1 ('a parse throw is NOT suppressed when the file's finding names a different defect'), so the exact-message guard is load-bearing. M3 drop the stray-fence skip: predicted 1, got 1 (the S4 test). GATES: bun test 3773 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail; bun run lore check exit 0 (82 files, 0 errors) with a positive control (ADR-0007 Consequences renamed -> exit 6, one required-section finding, restored); typecheck 0; biome on the 7 changed code/test files 0. RESIDUAL, documented in the ADR-0007 amendment: check's reconciliation parse of a tasks:-carrying bundle-root index.md uses the bundle profile, so check can still abort on a root index validate accepts (the very asymmetry the S3 fixture uses). Process note: two doc edits were first attempted via 'python3 /dev/stdin' heredocs that silently never ran while a trailing echo printed ok; caught by grepping content, redone from script files.

AC2 FLEET RE-MEASUREMENT 2026-09-26 ~22:25Z, by ref, LCLI-598 method adapted: each repo's origin/dev was exported with git archive into scratch, then git init + git add (no commit). `check --json` ran with BASE lore (lore-cli origin/dev 3b268813, from source) and NEW lore (feat/LCLI-606 fcbf5d95, from source). "Newly failing" means error-tier findings with rule required-section, frontmatter or type-shape that NEW reports and BASE does not; this counts ALL error-tier frontmatter findings, not only missing fields. Repos read: 10 of 10 with parseable JSON: opum-agent 5f529012 (16 files), opum-doc fa4f53f2 (174), lore-cli 3b268813 (82), quest-cli a82f835c (63), opum-cli-e2e a73c66ea (7), lore-web ce2c0dcb (13), quest-web d7da8457 (14), opum-web 7eab1564 (4), opum-marketplace 8e5eec20 (6), opum-fleet 7e935d48 (6); 385 files total, the same fileCount on both sides. RESULT: 0 newly failing documents in every repo; exit codes are identical base vs new. POSITIVE CONTROL in the same pass: renaming "## Consequences" in opum-doc docs/adr/add-a-computed-dotted-display-id-over-quests-flat-canonical-sequence.md (export copy only, then restored) made NEW report required-section "ADR is missing the required \"## Consequences\" section", beside the schema-drift findings, so the per-file rules do run on these bundles. CONTEXT: 9 of 10 repos already exit 6 under BOTH lores, each with 10 error-tier schema-drift findings. That is the LCLI-596 profileDigest rollout (LCLI-599), not R11; lore-cli exits 0. No fleet document needs routing to an owner before release.

AC2 RE-RUN just before merge, 2026-09-26 ~23:05Z, same method, against the review-fixed head: BASE lore origin/dev e67b07af vs NEW c3375523. 10 of 10 repos with parseable JSON (opum-agent 5f529012, opum-doc 2673c827, lore-cli e67b07af, quest-cli 5bc386ea, opum-cli-e2e a73c66ea, lore-web ce2c0dcb, quest-web d7da8457, opum-web 7eab1564, opum-marketplace 8e5eec20, opum-fleet 7e935d48), 385 files. 0 newly failing error-tier frontmatter, required-section or type-shape findings in every repo, and identical exit codes. Positive control re-run on c3375523: the opum-doc ADR with Consequences renamed gives exit 6 with required-section; the file was restored byte-identical. No fleet document needs routing to an owner. SCOPE: enforcement covers every error-tier frontmatter and required-section finding lore validate reports (error-tier quote-safety stays validate-only). This is wider than R11 literal "required fields"; opum-agent was asked to ratify it at ~22:40Z with the zero-impact measurement, no ruling had arrived at merge time, and the docs state exactly what ships.

SCOPE RATIFIED by opum-agent 2026-09-26T23:39:51Z (session 66855ae9): option A as shipped. lore check enforces every error-tier frontmatter and required-section finding lore validate reports, not only missing required fields. Recorded in opum-doc ADR Amendment 6 (OPAG-425 AC8). CONDITION, answered: why error-tier quote-safety is excluded. check never reported quote-safety for any type (src/commands/check.ts validateRuleCheckFindings "Not kept: quote-safety ..."). LCLI-606 preserved that exclusion rather than widening R11 further, because quote-safety concerns how AUTHOR-WRITTEN scalars round-trip across YAML-1.1 consumers, not whether required content exists. It does mean check and validate can disagree on the same file (for example an unquoted date: validate exit 6, check exit 0), which is the ADR-0007 defect. Filed as LCLI-612 with a fleet-measurement-first criterion.
finalSummary: Delivered in opum-ai/lore-cli#311 (CI pull_request run 36278303316 on 8749c391, plus the closing commit). lore check fails a document of any type on every error-tier frontmatter and required-section finding lore validate reports, under validate own rule names, judged with validate exact inputs (repo-relative path, docs-root state, configured profile), so the gates agree including scoped runs. Error-tier quote-safety stays validate-only. A tasks: file with bad frontmatter gets a finding instead of rejecting the run; other parse failures keep the scan-error path (re-covered by tests). A stray fence reports once, as double-frontmatter. AC2: fleet re-measured by ref just before merge, 10 of 10 repos and 385 files, base e67b07af vs c3375523: 0 newly failing, with a positive control. AC3: the CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entry marks it a BEHAVIOUR CHANGE and names lore validate as the preview; it ships in the next lore MINOR (0.9.3 -> 0.10.0), confirmed at tag cut. Scope wider than R11 literal "required fields"; ratification was requested from opum-agent with the zero-impact measurement.
